chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdus, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Layth al-Muradi, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about al-qasamah: upon whom is it—upon the family of the killer or upon the family of the slain?
He said: "It is upon the family of the slain; they swear by Allah, besides Whom there is no god, that so-and-so certainly killed so-and-so."

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْقَاتِلِ: the family or people associated with the alleged killer
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the family or people associated with the slain person
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: the formal oath procedure used in homicide cases
key_terms.بِاللَّهِ: by Allah, invoking Him in the oath
key_terms.لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ: there is no god except Him, a formula of solemn oath

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, upon whom does al-qasamah fall in a murder case?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling of al-qasamah in a homicide case. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that the oath is upon the family of the slain, who swear by Allah that a specified person killed the victim. The narration is significant in the law of judicial procedure and evidentiary rulings related to killing.
